spec_doc: docs/specs/gig-runs-once.red-spec.json — engine half of the two-repo fix; the store half (coltrane_drain_renew / coltrane_drain_release, attempts/max_attempts, terminal-status guard on the header upsert, lease clearing on terminal writes, manifest merge) lands in eir-labs/coltrane-ui branch work/gig-runs-once and deploys first. CONTRACT SURFACE the laws pin — src/lease.ts: export const HOSTED_LEASE_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000; export const DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES = { renew: '/rest/v1/rpc/coltrane_drain_renew', release: '/rest/v1/rpc/coltrane_drain_release' }; renew: POST ${COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL}${DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES.renew} body {p_gig_id} ONLY, Bearer drain key (the route fills p_token), X-Coltrane-Instance (the route fills p_instance); 200 -> new lease_until; 403 / 42501 -> lease lost; release: POST ${COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL}${DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES.release} body {p_gig_id, p_reason, p_terminal} ONLY, instance in X-Coltrane-Instance -> boolean; WorkOnceDeps.scheduleHeartbeat: (intervalMs: number, beat: () => Promise<unknown>) => () => void; default arms an unref'd setInterval; interval = HOSTED_LEASE_MS / 3; WorkOnceResult.acknowledged: boolean on a claimed result: true iff the store acknowledged the terminal header; terminal header attempts: 3; header status: 'running' is a new GigHeaderRecord status, sent awaited before the first chair with the run's genome_hash; manifest.cold_run_reason: string on a header written by a run that went cold because a resume was refused. ROUND 2: output drains are acknowledged (3 attempts) before the completed header; a 'running' header refused with 23514 or 403/42501 aborts the run with no terminal write. ROUND 3 (branch work/gig-runs-once-r3): G1 the heartbeat stays armed until the terminal header is acknowledged or exhausted; G2 no release after the outcome is decided when the terminal header is unacknowledged; REFUND a non-terminal release only before the first chair invocation; Q6 the drain deadline ends a gig aborted/timeout (WorkOnceResult status 'aborted', aborted:{reason:'timeout'}, header status 'aborted', no gig_fail); G4 (terminal rows only; founder ruling, Eugene: "what's closed is closed. can refer to the sealed outputs on input if needed but reopening doesn't smell right."): the successful resume path at gig_dispatch(resume_gig_id) / `coltrane dispatch --resume` runs today under the OLD id (gigId = resumeArg ?? randomUUID()), which the store's terminal guard answers with 23514; a resume of a failed/aborted gig must dispatch a NEW gig carrying resumes:<old id>, take the old seals as inputs by reference (content_sha in input_shas, never re-sealed), and write nothing under the old id. The refused-resume case is covered by tests/resume_reuse_dispatch.test.ts:164. A parked → approved → re-claimed gig is not terminal and keeps its id (E6b records a cold run there).

testing_method: vitest, example-based and behavioural: every engine law drives workOnce (or runCli / openLocalQueue) through a stubbed global fetch that plays both hosts — the org store (ctx.baseUrl RPCs) and the drain service (COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL: header, outputs, storage, renew, release) — statefully, so a re-claim reads what the first worker's acknowledged writes left behind. The heartbeat's clock is injected (WorkOnceDeps.scheduleHeartbeat) and fired from inside the chair invocation; acknowledgement is observed by holding the store's answer back (a delayed Response) and asserting what had resolved when workOnce returned. E8 moves the lease constant with vi.doMock over src/lease.ts and asserts both derived numbers follow. New symbols are reached by variable specifiers and casts so tsc over tests/ stays clean.
